entities.summary:
Michael Haddad (b. 1978), a Lebanese professional athlete, social entrepreneur, and prominent climate activist, has carved a unique niche as a global advocate for environmental protection and sustainable development. Known as 'The Ice Man' or 'The Snow Man' for his extraordinary endurance feats in extreme conditions, Haddad leverages his physical prowess to draw international attention to the urgency of climate action, particularly within the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. His work transcends conventional sports, integrating athleticism with public advocacy, making him a distinctive figure in contemporary environmental movements and a regional goodwill ambassador for the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

Throughout his career, Haddad has undertaken a series of record-breaking, physically demanding challenges designed to symbolize humanity's resilience and vulnerability in the face of environmental degradation. These include a 2020 3-kilometer walk through Lebanon's Cedars of God forest in sub-zero temperatures, performed with paralysis in one leg, to highlight the impacts of climate change on biodiversity. In 2021, he completed a 10-kilometer Arctic walk in -30°C to support the UNDP's climate initiatives, followed by a 100-kilometer desert run in Abu Dhabi to advocate for sustainable energy. His highly publicized 'Walk for a Cause' campaigns consistently link extreme physical endurance to specific environmental objectives, mobilizing public opinion and engaging policymakers.
